info.title: DigitalService API
info.description: Multi-tenant Go/Gin + MongoDB travel API. All GET requests are open reads: tenant-scoped ones (destinations, blogs, cars, packages, and every `/admin/*` list/get) only need `X-API-Key` to identify the tenant, and platform-level ones (`/platform/tenants`, `/platform/admins`, `/platform/projects`, `/platform/reviews`, `/platform/packages`, `/platform/quotes`) need no auth at all. Every mutating request (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) still requires the appropriate auth: `X-API-Key` for tenant-scoped writes, additionally a Bearer token with the `admin` role for `/admin/*` writes, and a Bearer token with the `superadmin` role for `/platform/*` writes — except `POST /platform/quotes`, deliberately open with no auth at all (see below). Tenant-scoped writes also pass through SubscriptionMiddleware — a tenant with an inactive/expired subscription gets 402 — except the six customer-facing lead/capture forms (`/bookings`, `/rentals`, `/airport-transfers`, `/contact`, `/quotes`, `/newsletter`), which are always accepted regardless of subscription state. If a tenant has a `domain` set (see `PUT /platform/tenants/{id}/domain`), every tenant-scoped request also passes through domain-bound key validation: a request carrying an `Origin` or `Referer` header that doesn't match that domain is rejected with 403, even with a valid `X-API-Key` — this only applies to browser-originated requests, since server-to-server calls send neither header. `Package` is a platform-wide catalog managed only via `/platform/packages` (not tenant-owned) — which tenants show a given package on their own storefront is a separate many-to-many assignment, `TenantPackage`, managed via `/platform/tenants/{id}/packages`; the tenant-scoped `/packages` reads are filtered through that assignment. A tenant's `Subscription.package_id` references the same `Package` catalog (typically the platform operator's own price list) — see `POST /platform/tenants/{id}/subscription`. `/platform/reviews` (TenantReview) are testimonials *from* the platform's own onboarded tenants for the operator's own Review page — distinct from tenant-scoped `/reviews` (a tenant's own customers reviewing that tenant's tours/partners). `Quote.tenant_id` is optional — a quote is a lead for a *potential* tenant, not every one has (or ever gets) an existing tenant relationship, so `POST /platform/quotes` accepts tenant-less leads with no auth at all, alongside the existing tenant-scoped `POST /quotes` (which does set `tenant_id`, from the X-API-Key); `GET /platform/quotes` and `PUT /platform/quotes/{id}/status` work across both.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Identifies the tenant. Format sk_live_<64 hex>, shown once at tenant creation / rotate-key. If the tenant has a domain set, this key is only accepted from requests whose Origin/Referer matches it (see PUT /platform/tenants/{id}/domain).

BearerAuth.description: Carries user_id, role, tenant_id. Obtained from /login (tenant users) or /platform/login (superadmin).

Unauthorized.description: Missing/invalid API key or bearer token

Forbidden.description: Token role/tenant does not match what this route requires

PaymentRequired.description: Tenant subscription is inactive or expired

Lang.name: lang
Lang.description: Locale for translatable fields. Falls back to the Accept-Language header, then to "en" if omitted or unsupported.

post.description: Invalidates the old key immediately.

put.description: Binds this tenant's X-API-Key to a domain. Once set, TenantMiddleware rejects requests whose Origin/Referer doesn't match it, even with a valid key. Stored lowercase, without scheme/path/port.

Partial update ($set) into this tenant's record in the separate tenant_details table (its "Our Projects" case-study content: tagline, description, category, website_url, cover_image, admin_cover, images, metrics, showcase, featured, sort_order) — deliberately a different table from the tenant's own identity/billing fields (status, domain, api key), which keep their own dedicated routes and are never touched by this one. Only the fields present in the body are changed; omitted fields are left as-is (matching the partial-update behavior of PUT /admin/partners/{id} etc.) — locale-map fields can be set per-locale via dot notation, e.g. `{"tagline.mn": "..."}`. website_url is the project's own live site shown as `live_url` on the public read (falling back to the tenant's bound Domain if unset); admin_cover is a separate image curated for front-page/list display, independent of cover_image (the case-study detail page's hero banner). Set showcase to true for the tenant to appear on GET /platform/projects, and the saved record is also embedded as `project` on GET /platform/tenants and /platform/tenants/{id}.

Public — no auth required. Joins active tenants against their tenant_details record where showcase=true, sorted by sort_order. This is the "Our Projects" storefront listing — a distinct, curated, locale-resolved read from GET /platform/tenants, which stays the platform's own full-detail tenant management view (contact_email, status, api_key_last4, and the raw `project` object included) and is unfiltered by showcase. tagline/description/metric labels are resolved to a single locale per `lang`.

The case-study detail page. `live_url` is the project's website_url if set, otherwise falls back to the tenant's bound domain (see PUT /platform/tenants/{id}/domain). `admin_cover` is a separate, front-page-curated image distinct from `cover_image` (the detail page's hero banner).
Public — no auth required. Active testimonials only. Returns just what the Review page needs: id, rate, comment, company_name, company_owner_name. comment is resolved to a single locale per `lang`.

post.description: package_id must reference an existing Package document (see /admin/packages) — typically one belonging to the platform operator's own tenant, i.e. its own price list sold to onboard other tenants. 400 if the package doesn't exist, 409 if the tenant already has a subscription. Status starts active with a 30-day period.

get.description: Public — no auth required. The response embeds the resolved `package` object (null if it was since deleted) alongside `package_id`. Includes `lastEditedBy` — the display name of the platform superadmin who last created/updated it (not a tenant user, since subscriptions are only ever managed via /platform routes) — when known.

put.description: package_id must reference an existing Package document. Starts a fresh 30-day billing period.

post.description: Sets status to canceled; package/period left intact. From this point the tenant's own writes get 402 until a superadmin sets a new package.
